analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows - Chart Pack (16 October 2026)
key_insights: Aggregate equity positioning edged lower but remains modestly overweight at 0.17sd (51st percentile). Discretionary positioning cut modestly to -0.36sd (24th percentile), further underweight. Systematic strategies were largely unchanged at 0.81sd (86th percentile).
Large caps declined but remain overweight (0.39sd, 69th percentile). Small caps moved deeper underweight (-0.69sd, 16th percentile).

Sector positioning is modestly overweight in MCG & Tech (0.18sd, 40th percentile, declined notably), Energy (0.15sd, 74th percentile, flipped from underweight) and Health Care (0.03sd, 54th percentile). It is underweight elsewhere.

Consumer Cyclicals positioning fell sharply from modestly overweight to underweight (-0.25sd, 57th percentile). Financials (-0.73sd, 11th percentile) and Industrial Cyclicals (-0.59sd, 21st percentile) fell sharply and sit near the bottom of their historical ranges.
Materials (-0.29sd, 21st percentile), Utilities (-0.27sd, 34th percentile), Consumer Staples (-0.27sd, 13th percentile) and Real Estate (-0.24sd, 51st percentile) remain underweight.

Call-to-put volume ratio (5d ma) declined modestly (77th percentile) as lower index option volume more than offset higher ETF and single-stock option volume. The single-stock decline was largest in MCG & Tech, with a smaller decline in Financials. S&P 500 3m 90%-110% skew rose.
The basket of stocks with the highest net call volume in the prior week and the basket of most shorted stocks both underperformed the broader market this week.

AAII sentiment turned slightly bearish (bull minus bear spread at 30th percentile). Bullish responses are at the 56th percentile, neutral at the 8th and bearish at the 84th, with bearish rising modestly.

Vol control funds' equity allocation declined but remains elevated (98th percentile). Their sensitivity to selloffs rose sharply, so capacity to add exposure is limited and the flow backdrop is less supportive if volatility rises.
CTA equity positioning declined but remains overweight (66th percentile). Exposure is high in Europe (76th percentile) and EM (77th percentile) and rose in the US (72nd percentile).

CTA positioning in other assets: bond shorts are extreme (US 11th percentile, Europe 12th percentile), dollar longs are elevated (97th percentile), gold is short (15th percentile), and copper (97th percentile) and oil (79th percentile) are notably long.

Risk parity equity allocations rose (80th percentile) across the US (85th), developed ex-US (81st) and EM (71st). Bond allocations are below norms (30th percentile). Commodity exposure rose to the 97th percentile. REIT (86th) and inflation-hedge (80th) exposure declined but remains elevated.

Weekly equity fund inflows accelerated sharply to $64.5bn, led by the US ($39.1bn) and EM ($17.7bn). Broad-global funds took in $8.2bn, Europe saw -$1.5bn of outflows, and Latam's $2.2bn was its largest on record.
Within EM, Asia ex-Japan took $14.9bn, including Taiwan ($5.5bn) and Korea ($1.1bn).

Sector fund flows: Tech took $10.7bn, the highest in 11 weeks. Energy ($1.3bn) and Health Care ($1.2bn) had their highest inflows in five and three months. Industrials lost $1.6bn, the biggest weekly outflow in over 12 years. Financials lost $1.4bn for a second week.
Bond fund inflows slowed to $11.8bn, the lowest in four weeks. Government bonds took $3.6bn and IG funds $2.8bn. Munis took $4.5bn, a record. HY (-$0.9bn) and MBS (-$0.9bn) had outflows.
Money market funds had outflows of $53.1bn, driven by the US (-$56.2bn), after massive inflows the prior week.
DB lists Moving Tech From Overweight To Neutral (Oct 9 2026) among its recent publications. Its S&P 500 2026 target is 8000, with 2026 EPS of $358 and 2027 EPS of $420.
Equity L/S hedge fund beta to the S&P 500 is at the 92nd percentile (1m) and 90th percentile (3m). Large cap mutual fund beta is at the 71st percentile (1m) and 16th percentile (3m).
Total net call volume (5d ma) is at the 98th percentile since 2010.
Bond futures positioning as % of open interest is net short across maturities: SOFR -18.8%, 2y -20.0%, 5y -15.7%, 10y -14.2%, 30y -6.8%, Ultra -13.4%.
CTA currency positioning percentiles are low for EUR (4%), CAD (1%), CHF (6%), GBP (2%) and NZD (1%), and AUD is at 70%.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning is modestly overweight (0.18sd, 40th percentile) but declined notably. Sector funds took in $10.7bn, the highest in 11 weeks.
Positioning flipped to modestly overweight (0.15sd, 74th percentile) and fund inflows of $1.3bn were the highest in five months.
Positioning is just above neutral (0.03sd, 54th percentile). Fund inflows of $1.2bn were the highest in three months.
Positioning fell sharply to -0.73sd (11th percentile), near the bottom of its range. Funds had outflows for a second straight week (-$1.4bn).
Industrial Cyclicals positioning is -0.59sd (21st percentile). Funds had the biggest weekly outflow in over 12 years (-$1.6bn).
Positioning dropped sharply from modestly overweight to -0.25sd (57th percentile).

risk_factors: Vol control funds are at the 98th percentile of equity allocation with higher sensitivity to selloffs, so a volatility rise would bring a less supportive flow backdrop.
Systematic positioning is stretched at the 86th percentile, which limits capacity to add exposure.
Discretionary investors are underweight at the 24th percentile and small caps are deeply underweight at the 16th percentile.
Financials and Industrial Cyclicals positioning has fallen close to the bottom of historical ranges.
